text:
jules: Quick thought: what if the routing decision can see a lightweight 'warmness' signal from the serving plane so we bias towards nodes that already have the model's KV/prefix cached? Could cut p50 by a few tens of ms and reduce cross-region egress.

amir: Are you proposing a boolean "has_cache" or a graded metric? Also need to ensure we never violate tenant region constraints or data residency.

jules: Graded. Call it local_kv_hotness (0-100). It should be advisory only.

tara: Two parts to consider: (1) how sidecars publish this without insane cardinality, (2) how policy compiler treats the field.

amir: Runtime work: sidecar aggregates rolling hit_rate and avg_kv_fetch_ms. We publish aggregated per-(model,region,instance_class) every 60s. For tenants that opt-in we can add a tenant-mask sample if needed.

ops-bot: Reminder: any new route attribute must be behind a feature flag and have a canary checklist. Suggested flag: ENABLE_LOCAL_CACHE_HINTS.

jules: Policy semantics proposal: add route attribute 'local_kv_hotness' as an optional numeric. Rules may add a small soft score bump if hotness>threshold. Compiler MUST prevent converting this into a hard constraint (no '== true' style rules).

amir: Edge case: what if the hot route is overloaded CPU/GPU-wise? We need to feed current capacity metrics alongside hotness, otherwise we will oscillate to hot but saturated nodes.

rick: Good point. Suggest combining 'local_kv_hotness' with 'route_load_pct' and let scoring be: score = base - alpha*load + beta*hotness. Beta tuned small. Also add a dampening window to avoid flip-flopping.

tara: TTL/consistency issue: some KV entries are short-lived. We should include 'sample_ts' and 'estimated_ttl_ms' so policy can decay hotness as TTL approaches zero. Otherwise stale embeddings could be served.

jules: Data-model suggestion for the route proto (optional field): "local_kv_hint" stringified proto e.g. "hotness=82;sample_ts=5109876500;ttl_ms=300000;agg=region". Keep it compact to limit proto churn.

amir: I'd rather add a small typed struct: {hotness, sample_ts, ttl_ms, agg_key}. But ok, we can minify. Compiler will parse.

ops-bot: Note: telemetry cardinality risk flagged. Prefer aggregated per (model,region) with optional tenant_mask for top N tenants. Retention 1h for this metric to limit cost.

rick: Testing plan: simulation harness with a fleet model: synthetic hotness and load traces, validate oscillation under different beta/alpha and dampening windows. Add unit tests that ensure policies with hard_affinity flags ignore hotness.

tara: Rollout plan: behind ENABLE_LOCAL_CACHE_HINTS, staged rollout: single region (us-east-1) small percentage of traffic, 6h soak -> cross-region canary -> 24h. Monitors: p50,p95 latency, cross-region egress, routing churn rate, model error rates. Also instrument "decision_reason" when hotness changes route chosen.

amir: Operational requirement: sidecar should fail-open: if it can't publish hotness, routes behave as today. No single-point dependency.

jules: Security & compliance: any tenant-plumbing that causes cross-region must be validated against tenant settings. Hotness must never override 'region_pin' or 'data_residency' tags. Compiler lint to enforce.

ops-bot: Action items: jules -> write design doc + sample proto; amir -> sidecar publish PR + config knobs for aggregation; tara -> compiler lint + policy rule examples; rick -> simulation harness and unit tests. Add feature flag to infra ticket.

rick: I'll sketch a decay curve and share simulated numbers for hotness half-life in the 2-10 minute range. Also will add a dampening token bucket to policy so repeated switches are rate-limited.

amir: I'll also include a small proof-of-concept payload we can test: {"model":"stable-v1","region":"us-east-1","hotness":0.78,"avg_kv_ms":2.1,"ts":5109876490}.

tara: Keep decision traces for 7 days (index minimal fields) so we can tune thresholds offline.

jules: Thanks all. If no objections I'll turn this into an RFC draft with the suggested proto and rollout checklist. :raised_hands: 

ops-bot: Reminder: link RFC to ops checklist and schedule canary with SRE.
